solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Husband with applause

parts.note: and means together with, the same joining sense as with

explanation.surface: A husband joins in clapping at some performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a big hand is to clap them, so this word stands for a round of clapping.

clue.text: Get rid of nasty boils in a hospital

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters inside the other two pieces

parts.note: H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: nasty boils suggests the letters of boils are messed up

explanation.surface: Treating unpleasant skin sores in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges BOILS to OLIS, set by 'in' between A and H.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to do away with something entirely, a synonym of eliminate.

clue.text: Beginning to drink a tea in country cottage

indicators.note: beginning to drink means its first letter

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Starting on a cuppa in a rural retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian holiday house in the countryside, a kind of rural cottage.

clue.text: Shameful shout we hear in game

parts.note: base means morally low, dishonourable

indicators.note: we hear tells us the next word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to bawl is to shout loudly

explanation.surface: Someone yells something disgraceful during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' covers only the shout: the word for yelling is spelt differently from the round object a pitcher throws.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is the American bat-and-ball sport, an example of a game.

clue.text: Save in bank

definitions.meaning: save in the sense of except, as in all save one
a sandbank in a river or sea, a raised ridge of sand

explanation.surface: Putting money away at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the preposition meaning except; the other is a sandbank off a coast.

clue.text: Proudly display evidence of accident, in fast vehicle

parts.note: to sport something is to wear or show it off proudly
a scar is the mark left by an injury

explanation.surface: Someone shows off crash damage on a speedy motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports car is a fast two-seater built for performance, a quick vehicle.

clue.text: Sort of map shown in manual on a weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
shown in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a manual is a handbook, a book
an A-Z is a London street-map book, so the term names a kind of map

explanation.surface: A map appears in a handbook about some weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is a British street atlas, a city map book.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazooka is a portable anti-tank rocket launcher, a military weapon.

clue.text: Weapon's spike catching knight

definitions.note: Weapon's stands for weapon is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: catching means holding another piece inside

parts.note: to spike a drink is to lace it with alcohol
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A weapon's sharp point snags a mounted warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spike' looks like a point but means doctor a drink. The definition is 'Weapon', with 's for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long pointed pole carried by jousting knights, a classic weapon.

clue.text: Piece of music from show, last in 'Chicago'

parts.note: a concert is a musical show or performance

indicators.note: last in asks for the final letter of the word Chicago

explanation.surface: A number taken from a show, the final one in the musical Chicago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicago' looks like the musical, but only its final letter O is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a composition for soloist and orchestra, a kind of musical work.

clue.text: Close to Jerez, unique region

indicators.note: close here means the end, so close to Jerez is its final letter

parts.note: one can mean unique, as in one of a kind

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind area lying near the Spanish town of Jerez.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as near, but here it means the end of Jerez.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is an area or district, a synonym for a region.

clue.text: From Mavis, an endorsement

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, inside them

explanation.surface: A woman called Mavis gives her backing to something.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official stamp on a passport approving entry, a form of endorsement.

clue.text: Worked out carrying much weight in diamonds

parts.note: someone carrying much weight is fat
in can mean at home, as in 'is she in?'
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone heavily laden with jewels has solved a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but supplies HOME, as in staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to understand it, so the past tense means figured out.

clue.text: Female is on Channel Island with an angler

parts.note: Herm is one of the small Channel Islands, near Guernsey

explanation.surface: A woman is on a Channel Island with someone fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Herm is a small island between England and France, by Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler catches fish with rod and line, so he or she is one who fishes.

clue.text: Ancient city he bets is in a destroyed state

indicators.note: letters in a destroyed state are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A gambler wagers that some old city lies in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a famous city of ancient Egypt and also one of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Illegally made kick on limb

parts.note: to boot is to kick
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A kick lands on someone's leg in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg goods are produced or sold unlawfully, such as smuggled spirits or pirate recordings.

clue.text: Greatly pleases church members

parts.note: arms are limbs, and member is an old word for a limb

explanation.surface: A congregation delights the people who belong to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' suggests congregation, but it means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to delight them, so the verb in this form matches pleases greatly.

clue.text: Note what Tuscany has?

parts.note: Tuscany is in the middle of Italy, and the middle letter of the word Tuscany is C, the musical note

explanation.surface: Asking what the Italian region of Tuscany possesses.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical note sits at the centre of the piano keyboard, and C is the central letter of Tuscany.

clue.text: Sure boat at sea is a wrecker?

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A vessel out on the ocean is surely a ship that wrecks others.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately damages things, so wrecker describes one, with the question mark for the loose fit.

clue.text: Friend, male one in past

indicators.note: in puts the two pieces inside the word for past

parts.note: ago means in the past
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A former mate, a man from years gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, borrowed into English for a pal.

clue.text: Chapter and verse in secret language

parts.note: an ode is a poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: Citing chapter and verse, as from scripture, in hidden speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chapter and verse' is a set phrase but splits into C and a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a system of symbols for concealing messages, a cipher or secret language.

clue.text: US soldier climbing in automobile finds smoke

indicators.note: in puts the turned piece inside the other

parts.note: a car is an automobile

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means read upward, backwards

parts.note: GI is the usual name for an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier getting into a car lights up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' works because this is a down clue, so a backwards reading runs upward; 'in' marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is rolled tobacco for smoking, so it can be called a smoke.

clue.text: Work the land — there may be money in it

definitions.meaning: to cultivate soil by ploughing, as a farmer does

definitions.text: there may be money in it
definitions.meaning: a shop's cash drawer, where takings are kept

explanation.surface: Farming could turn a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is ploughing ground for crops; the other is a cash register drawer.

clue.text: Flower girl mad, crazy to consume nothing

indicators.note: to consume means to swallow, so one piece goes inside the other
crazy says the letters of girl mad are scrambled

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A frantic young woman refuses to eat at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges GIRL MAD, and 'to consume' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The marigold is a yellow or orange garden bloom, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Deserter, sailor, capsized

indicators.note: capsized means turned over, so the word is read upward in this down clue

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who jumped ship had his boat overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is someone who abandons a cause, from rats leaving a sinking ship.

clue.text: Money the head required for food item

parts.note: dough is slang for money
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A boss needs cash to buy something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughnut is a fried ring or ball of sweet dough, an edible treat.

clue.text: Runs excellent sprint

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone runs a superb dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a short fast running contest, so it is a kind of race.
